posture_summary.text: Spain operates as a European middle power characterized by multi-vector positioning that leverages institutional buffers to maintain political agency disproportionate to its material weight. The Adamuz train disaster has become a focal point for direct victims' family confrontation with government credibility while the opposition internationalizes domestic crises through European People's Party channels. Spain's migration regularization policy (500,000 undocumented migrants) creates friction with EU partners while domestic opposition uses 'invasion' rhetoric that threatens democratic discourse norms. The March 2026 denial of US base access continues to define Spain's distinctive approach within NATO—maintaining alliance membership while asserting independence on military operations—as evidenced by continued defense cooperation through routine modernization programs including $1.42 billion in approved frigate upgrades.
